sentences.zh: 所以正如你所说，汤姆，

sentences.en: So Göring, Göring's a funny man, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 所以戈林，戈林是个有趣的人，不是吗？

sentences.en: He's a strange man.
sentences.zh: 他是个怪人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Henderson, Beck and Göring, they'd all had a great time going shooting things.
sentences.zh: 亨德森、贝克和戈林，他们以前都很喜欢去打猎。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Can I just ask, Czechoslovakia was a democracy.
sentences.zh: 我能问一下吗，捷克斯洛伐克当时是个民主国家。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And presumably that was part of why they were allies with Britain and France.
sentences.zh: 想必这也是他们与英法结盟的部分原因。

sentences.en: Is it important that Poland isn't?
sentences.zh: 波兰不是民主国家，这很重要吗？

sentences.en: Poland isn't.
sentences.zh: 波兰确实不是。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Is that an issue?
sentences.zh: 这是个问题吗？

sentences.en: I don't think it's a massive issue deep down, because, of course, there are lots of countries at this point that are not democracies.
sentences.zh: 我觉得从根本上来说这不是什么大问题，因为当然了，当时有很多国家都不是民主国家。

sentences.en: And I think it would have been an easier sell if it was.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为如果它是民主国家，会更容易被接受。

sentences.en: But actually, the French, for example, the French are very polonophile and have been for a very long time.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，比如法国人，法国人非常亲波兰，而且已经持续很长时间了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Chopper.
sentences.zh: 乔珀。

sentences.en: They regard themselves as having a kind of special relationship with Poland.
sentences.zh: 他们认为自己与波兰有一种特殊关系。

sentences.en: And in Britain, do people say, oh, the Poles, really?
sentences.zh: 而在英国，人们会说，哦，波兰人，真的吗？

sentences.en: They're not a democracy?
sentences.zh: 他们不是民主国家？

sentences.en: I don't think they do, actually.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他们其实不会这么想。

sentences.en: I don't think they give it that much thought deep down.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他们从心底里没怎么考虑过这个问题。

sentences.en: They don't really care anything about the Poles.
sentences.zh: 他们根本不在乎波兰人。

sentences.en: I don't think they really care what kind of government they have.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他们并不在乎波兰是什么样的政府。

sentences.en: The interesting thing is what Hitler and the Germans make of the Poles.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是希特勒和德国人是怎么看待波兰人的。

sentences.en: So, most Germans hold the Poles in very, very low regard.
sentences.zh: 所以，大多数德国人对波兰人的评价非常非常低。

sentences.en: So, in the 19th century, when a lot of Poland, of course, had been part of the Wilhelm Einreich, the Kaiser's regime, they had looked down on the Poles.
sentences.zh: 在19世纪，当波兰大部分地区当然是德意志帝国，也就是德皇政权的一部分时，他们就看不起波兰人。

sentences.en: Germans had said, well, the Poles are very backward.
sentences.zh: 德国人会说，嗯，波兰人非常落后。

sentences.en: The Poles are very superstitious.
sentences.zh: 波兰人非常迷信。

sentences.en: They're very stupid.
sentences.zh: 他们非常愚蠢。

sentences.en: They actually had an expression, Polandwirtschaft, a Polish business, which meant kind of muddle and incompetence.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至有一个词叫“Polandwirtschaft”，意为“波兰式经营”，指代混乱和无能。

sentences.en: You know, they sort of looked on them.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们就是那样看待他们的。

sentences.en: I suppose the analogy would be how people in the late 19th century in Britain talked about Ireland, actually, as a kind of, you know, oh, they can never govern themselves.
sentences.zh: 我想类比一下的话，就像19世纪末英国人谈论爱尔兰人的方式，你知道，哦，他们永远无法自我治理。

sentences.en: They're so disorganized and they're so backward and primitive and blah, blah, blah, blah, blah.
sentences.zh: 他们太混乱、太落后、太原始，诸如此类，巴拉巴拉。

sentences.en: That's how Germans think of the Poles.
sentences.zh: 这就是德国人对波兰人的看法。

sentences.en: Even in the 1920s, lots of Germans said, look, in the long run,
sentences.zh: 即使在20世纪20年代，许多德国人也说，看，从长远来看，

sentences.en: Poland will have to cease to exist again.
sentences.zh: 波兰将不得不再次消失。

sentences.en: There's no way we can live with a country called Poland on our eastern border.
sentences.zh: 我们不可能在东部边境上容忍一个叫波兰的国家存在。

sentences.en: I mean, the head of the army of the Weimar Republic, General Hans von Sieght in 1922, said, Poland's existence is intolerable and incompatible with Germany's vital interests.
sentences.zh: 我是说，魏玛共和国军队首脑汉斯·冯·塞克特将军在1922年曾说，波兰的存在是不可容忍的，与德国的根本利益不相容。

sentences.en: It must and it will disappear through its own weakness and, without help, through Russia.
sentences.zh: 它必须且终将因自身的软弱而消失，如果没有外力，也会因俄国而消失。

sentences.en: So even then, the Germans are thinking that perhaps they should carve it up with the Russians.
sentences.zh: 所以即使在那个时候，德国人也在想也许他们应该和俄国人瓜分它。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Because they have done before, like the partitions of the 1790s.
sentences.zh: 因为他们以前做过，就像18世纪90年代的瓜分波兰一样。

sentences.en: But even though it's actually, of course, not Russia anymore, it's the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 虽然现在当然已经不是俄国了，而是苏联。

sentences.en: But they think, you know, it's kind of the law of nature and of history that the Poles never govern themselves.
sentences.zh: 但他们认为，你知道，波兰人永远无法自我治理是自然和历史的法则。

sentences.en: A bit like, you know, the Kurds don't have a state.
sentences.zh: 有点像，你知道，库尔德人没有国家一样。

sentences.en: They'll be one of those people who never get a state of their own.
sentences.zh: 他们会是那些永远无法拥有自己国家的人民之一。

sentences.en: OK, and so one guy who's very keen on this idea that the strong must prey on the weak is Hitler.
sentences.zh: 好的，那么有一个非常热衷于“强者必须掠夺弱者”这一理念的人就是希特勒。

sentences.en: What is his take on the Poles?
sentences.zh: 他对波兰有什么看法？

sentences.en: Well, this is fascinating.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这很有趣。

sentences.en: Hitler, who, of course, later on is perceived as incredibly anti-Polish, he doesn't have a strong view about Poland at all before 1938.
sentences.zh: 希特勒，当然，后来被认为极其反波兰，但在1938年之前，他根本没有对波兰持有强烈的看法。

sentences.en: He barely mentions Poland in Mein Kampf.
sentences.zh: 他在《我的奋斗》中几乎没提到波兰。

sentences.en: And the obvious reason for this is that, of course, Hitler is not German.
sentences.zh: 显而易见的原因是，希特勒当然不是德国人。

sentences.en: I mean, Hitler is Austrian.
sentences.zh: 我是说，希特勒是奥地利人。

sentences.en: Yeah, he's much further south, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 是啊，他来自更南边，不是吗？

sentences.en: So that's why he hates the Czechs.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是他讨厌捷克人的原因。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So he never really thinks about the Poles.
sentences.zh: 所以他从没真正考虑过波兰人。

sentences.en: Why would he?
sentences.zh: 他为什么要考虑？

sentences.en: When he's in Vienna, the Galician Poles aren't massively playing on his mind.
sentences.zh: 当他在维也纳时，加利西亚的波兰人并没有占据他的心思。

sentences.en: He doesn't care.
sentences.zh: 他不在乎。

sentences.en: Think about Warsaw and all of that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 想想华沙和所有那些事情。

sentences.en: And actually, in January 1934, he had overruled conservatives in the Foreign Office to sign a non-aggression treaty with Poland because he wanted to secure his eastern flank.
sentences.zh: 实际上，在1934年1月，他推翻了外交部保守派的意见，与波兰签署了互不侵犯条约，因为他想确保东翼的安全。

sentences.en: But I mean, people are always talking about these non-aggression pacts and things.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，人们总是在谈论这些互不侵犯条约之类的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Meaningless.
sentences.zh: 毫无意义。

sentences.en: They are meaningless, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 它们毫无意义，不是吗？

sentences.en: They're totally meaningless.
sentences.zh: 它们完全没有意义。

sentences.en: They're not worth the paper they're written on.
sentences.zh: 它们甚至不值写在上面的那张纸钱。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不值。

sentences.en: Unless you're Neville Chamberlain, in which case you love a piece of paper.
sentences.zh: 除非你是内维尔·张伯伦，那样的话你就会喜欢那张纸。

sentences.en: But I think it's fair to say Adolf Hitler is not a man who adheres to a non-aggression pact.
sentences.zh: 但我认为可以公平地说，阿道夫·希特勒不是一个会遵守互不侵犯条约的人。

sentences.en: I think that's the one lesson we can all take from these three seasons on Nazis.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是我们从这三季关于纳粹的节目中能学到的唯一教训。

sentences.en: But generally, I mean, do other powers stick by them?
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，其他大国会遵守这些条约吗？

sentences.en: I mean, if the Soviet Union signs a non-aggression pact, for instance, I mean, were that to happen?
sentences.zh: 我是说，如果苏联签署了互不侵犯条约，比如，如果发生了这种情况？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Do they think, yeah, we should stick with this?
sentences.zh: 他们会想，是的，我们应该遵守这个吗？

sentences.en: Or is that kind of bourgeois legalism?
sentences.zh: 还是说那只是一种资产阶级的法律主义？

sentences.en: I think it depends on the country, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 我觉得这取决于国家，不是吗？

sentences.en: I think if I signed a non-aggression pact with Stalin, I wouldn't necessarily have a great bit of confidence in his word.
sentences.zh: 我想如果我和斯大林签署了互不侵犯条约，我未必会对他信守承诺抱有太大信心。

sentences.en: If I signed a non-aggression pact with Neville Chamberlain or Deladier...
sentences.zh: 如果我和内维尔·张伯伦或达拉第签署了互不侵犯条约……

sentences.en: Then you would.
sentences.zh: 那你会的。

sentences.en: I would.
sentences.zh: 我会的。

sentences.en: Wouldn't you?
sentences.zh: 难道不是吗？

sentences.en: Yes, I would.
sentences.zh: 是的，我会。

sentences.en: But I mean, all these non-aggression pact that everyone is furiously signing with Germany and the Soviet Union, I mean, it just seems a waste of effort.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，每个人都在疯狂地与德国和苏联签署这些互不侵犯条约，这看起来简直是浪费精力。

sentences.en: They've wasted their time, Tom, I think it's fair to say.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我想可以公平地说，他们浪费了时间。

sentences.en: Good.
sentences.zh: 很好。

sentences.en: I'm glad I've got that sorted.
sentences.zh: 很高兴我把这件事理清了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So what does Hitler want to do with Poland?
sentences.zh: 那么希特勒想对波兰做什么？

sentences.en: He's absolutely, even at the beginning of 1939, I'm not sure he's thinking about attacking and conquering it.
sentences.zh: 他绝对是，即使在1939年初，我不确定他是否在考虑攻击和征服它。

sentences.en: He's thinking that Poland will just be a satellite, basically turn it into a client state, which is what he does with Slovakia and what he does with Hungary.
sentences.zh: 他认为波兰只会是一个卫星国，基本上把它变成一个附庸国，就像他对斯洛伐克和匈牙利所做的那样。

sentences.en: Bind Poland to him as a loyal ally in the crusade against Bolshevism.
sentences.zh: 将波兰束缚在他身边，作为反布尔什维克十字军东征中的忠实盟友。

sentences.en: And actually, you can see why he thinks he could do that.
sentences.zh: 实际上，你可以看出他为什么认为自己能做到这一点。

sentences.en: They have an authoritarian nationalist regime.
sentences.zh: 他们有一个威权民族主义政权。

sentences.en: The Poles had rather let themselves down at Munich.
sentences.zh: 波兰人在慕尼黑会议上表现得相当令人失望。

sentences.en: Yeah, so Hitler's given them a chunk of Czechoslovakia.
sentences.zh: 是啊，所以希特勒给了他们一大块捷克斯洛伐克的领土。

sentences.en: He has.
sentences.zh: 他确实给了。

sentences.en: The old Silesian Duchy of Tesschen.
sentences.zh: 泰申的旧西里西亚公国。

sentences.en: Not the Silesian Duchy of Tesschen.
sentences.zh: 不是泰申的西里西亚公国。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: The Czechs and the Poles had fought each other for this in 1919.
sentences.zh: 捷克人和波兰人在1919年曾为此打过仗。

sentences.en: The Czechs had got it.
sentences.zh: 捷克人得到了它。

sentences.en: And then the Poles snatch it back at the end of 1938.
sentences.zh: 然后波兰人在1938年底把它抢了回来。

sentences.en: This actually makes them all pretty pro-German, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 这实际上让他们变得相当亲德，不是吗？

sentences.en: And they all kind of rush around Warsaw shouting out, long live Hitler.
sentences.zh: 他们都在华沙到处跑，高喊希特勒万岁。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And actually, there's a very famous moment.
sentences.zh: 实际上，有一个非常著名的时刻。

sentences.en: So, two days after Munich, they got it and the Poles went in and the Czech general who handed it over to them, he said to the Polish general, well,
sentences.zh: 在慕尼黑会议两天后，他们得到了它，波兰人进驻了，把领土移交给他们的捷克将军对波兰将军说，好吧，

sentences.en: you better make the most of this because I'll tell you what, you're going to be next.
sentences.zh: 你最好充分利用这一点，因为我告诉你，下一个就轮到你了。

sentences.en: And the Poles said, ha, ha, ha, that will never happen.
sentences.zh: 波兰人说，哈哈，那永远不会发生。

sentences.en: And how wrong they were.
sentences.zh: 他们错得有多离谱啊。

sentences.en: But anyway, three weeks after that moment, Ribbentrop asks the Polish ambassador, a man called Mr. Lipsky, to come and see him.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，在那一刻之后的三周，里宾特洛甫要求波兰大使，一个叫利普斯基的人，去见他。

sentences.en: And he says, we actually have a bit of a problem that we need to discuss.
sentences.zh: 他说，我们实际上有一个需要讨论的小问题。

sentences.en: You can imagine the blood draining from the Polish ambassador's face.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象波兰大使脸上的血色瞬间褪尽的样子。

sentences.en: So here is the problem.
sentences.zh: 所以问题就在这里。

sentences.en: After the First World War, when Poland had been carved out of these empires, the peacemakers of Versailles realized that Poland wasn't going to get any access to the sea at all.
sentences.zh: 第一次世界大战后，当波兰从这些帝国中被分割出来时，凡尔赛的缔造者们意识到波兰根本无法获得任何出海口。

sentences.en: Because it was on the northern flank of Poland.
sentences.zh: 因为它位于波兰的北翼。

sentences.en: It was all East Prussia, which is German, and Lithuania.
sentences.zh: 那里全是东普鲁士，也就是德国的领土，还有立陶宛。

sentences.en: And they realized that they needed to give Poland an hour left to the sea.
sentences.zh: 他们意识到需要给波兰一个出海口。

sentences.en: Otherwise, Germany in particular would have a complete stranglehold over Poland's trade, its exports and imports.
sentences.zh: 否则，德国尤其会对波兰的贸易、出口和进口拥有完全的控制权。

sentences.en: So they'd carved out this Polish corridor, as they called it, which is quite narrow.
sentences.zh: 所以他们开辟了这个所谓的波兰走廊，它相当狭窄。

sentences.en: The narrowest point is about 20 miles across.
sentences.zh: 最窄处大约只有20英里宽。

sentences.en: It went through West Prussia, so basically dividing Germany into two parts, into the main bit of the Reich and then East Prussia.
sentences.zh: 它穿过西普鲁士，基本上把德国分成了两部分，即帝国的主体部分和东普鲁士。

sentences.en: And there's the Polish corridor between them.
sentences.zh: 中间就是波兰走廊。

sentences.en: And that's not the kind of thing that Hitler would approve of, is it?
sentences.zh: 那不是希特勒会赞同的事情，对吧？

sentences.en: Not at all.
sentences.zh: 一点也不。

sentences.en: Because the population of the Polish corridor is mixed.
sentences.zh: 因为波兰走廊的人口是混合的。

sentences.en: It is majority Polish, probably.
sentences.zh: 可能大多数是波兰人。

sentences.en: I mean, this is very contested at the time by kind of rival census takers.
sentences.zh: 我是说，当时各方人口普查统计对此有很大争议。

sentences.en: But there's a very sizable German minority.
sentences.zh: 但那里有相当多的德国少数民族。

sentences.en: And at the north end of this corridor, on the coast, is the city of Danzig, or Dansk, as it is today.
sentences.zh: 在这个走廊的北端，在海岸上，是但泽市，也就是今天的格但斯克。

sentences.en: And there is no doubt what kind of city Danzig is.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，但泽是什么样的城市。

sentences.en: It is a Hanseatic League German city.
sentences.zh: 它是一座汉萨同盟的德国城市。

sentences.en: It looks kind of German.
sentences.zh: 它看起来很像德国城市。

sentences.en: Now, it had belonged to Poland.
sentences.zh: 它曾经属于波兰。

sentences.en: It had belonged to the Teutonic Knights.
sentences.zh: 它曾经属于条顿骑士团。

sentences.en: It had belonged to Poland again.
sentences.zh: 它又属于波兰。

sentences.en: And then it had belonged to Prussia.
sentences.zh: 然后它属于普鲁士。

sentences.en: The population of Danzig is definitely majority German-speaking, at least 90%.
sentences.zh: 但泽的人口绝对是以德语为母语的多数，至少占90%。

sentences.en: I mean, you can go to Gdansk today, which I have.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你可以去今天的格但斯克看看，我去过。

sentences.en: It's the most amazing city to visit.
sentences.zh: 那是一座非常令人惊叹的城市。

sentences.en: It's incredibly rich architecturally and in history and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 它在建筑、历史等方面极其丰富。

sentences.en: And it looks like a Hanseatic League city.
sentences.zh: 它看起来就像一座汉萨同盟城市。

sentences.en: However, you know, Poland needs its outlet on the sea.
sentences.zh: 然而，你知道，波兰需要它的出海口。

sentences.en: So, what the Versailles Peacemakers did was they made Danzig a free city, an independent city-state, under the supervision of the League of Nations.
sentences.zh: 凡尔赛和会的缔造者们将但泽设为自由市，即一个在国际联盟监督下的独立城邦。

sentences.en: So, very Hanseatic.
sentences.zh: 听起来很有汉萨同盟的风格。

sentences.en: Yeah, very Hanseatic.
sentences.zh: 没错，非常有汉萨同盟的感觉。

sentences.en: It was governed by a Senate, basically a German Senate.
sentences.zh: 它由一个参议院管理，基本上是一个德国人的参议院。

sentences.en: But the Poles had the right to use the harbour.
sentences.zh: 但波兰人有权使用该港口。

sentences.en: And they were given a post office there and customs posts.
sentences.zh: 他们还在那里获得了邮局和海关哨所。

sentences.en: And on this sort of peninsula across the harbour called the Westerplatte, which we'll be talking about a fair bit in the next couple of episodes,
sentences.zh: 在港口对面有一个半岛，叫西盘半岛，我们在接下来的几集里会经常提到它，

sentences.en: there was a Polish military garrison.
sentences.zh: 那里驻扎着波兰的军事守备队。

sentences.en: And this was a massive running soar.
sentences.zh: 这成了一个巨大的长期痛点。

sentences.en: This was a massive affront to German nationalist conservatives, especially if you're Prussian or something.
sentences.zh: 这对德国民族主义保守派来说是一种巨大的侮辱，尤其是如果你是普鲁士人或者有类似背景的话。

sentences.en: Because Danzig is a place in an important role in Prussian hearts?
sentences.zh: 是因为但泽在普鲁士人的心中占有重要地位吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: You're like, this is a Prussian city.
sentences.zh: 你会觉得，这就是一座普鲁士城市。

sentences.en: These people are Germans.
sentences.zh: 这里的人民是德国人。

sentences.en: It's not right that it's a free state.
sentences.zh: 它成为一个自由邦是不对的。

sentences.en: You know, it should really be part of the Reich.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它理应是帝国的一部分。

sentences.en: And who cares about the Poles?
sentences.zh: 谁在乎波兰人怎么想？

sentences.en: That's basically the German position.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是德国人的立场。

sentences.en: So, this is what Ribbentrop says to this ambassador.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是里宾特洛甫对那位大使说的话。

sentences.en: He says, right, we've had enough.
sentences.zh: 他说，好了，我们受够了。

sentences.en: We want Danzig back.
sentences.zh: 我们要收回但泽。

sentences.en: We also want to be able to build a motorway and a railway across the Polish corridor, which we control.
sentences.zh: 我们还希望能够修建一条穿过波兰走廊的高速公路和铁路，并由我们来控制。

sentences.en: We'll extend the non-aggression pact for another 25 years.
sentences.zh: 我们将把互不侵犯条约再延长25年。

sentences.en: Tom, I know your views on non-aggression pact.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我知道你对互不侵犯条约的看法。

sentences.en: That's a good deal.
sentences.zh: 那可是个好买卖。

sentences.en: And we'd like you to join the anti-commontern pact to basically bind you into our alliance, our anti-Bolshevik alliance.
sentences.zh: 而且我们希望你们加入《反共产国际协定》，基本上就是把你们纳入我们的联盟，我们的反布尔什维克联盟。

sentences.en: The Polish guy says, all right, well, I'll take this back to Warsaw, see what they say.
sentences.zh: 波兰人说，好吧，我会把这些带回华沙，看看他们怎么说。

sentences.en: And the Poles reply very quickly and they say, absolutely no way.
sentences.zh: 波兰人很快就回复了，他们说，绝对没门。

sentences.en: We can't allow ourselves to be cut off from the sea.
sentences.zh: 我们不能让自己被切断与海洋的联系。

sentences.en: They couldn't have built a road under the German motorway and railway.
sentences.zh: 他们本可以在德国高速公路和铁路下方修一条路啊。

sentences.en: What, they could have undermined it with a road of their own?
sentences.zh: 什么，他们本可以用自己的路从下面穿过去吗？

sentences.en: I mean, you'd have bridges.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你可以修桥啊。

sentences.en: You could have a Polish motorway over the...
sentences.zh: 你可以修一条波兰的高速公路跨过……

sentences.en: To be fair, it's not motorway architecture that is the pointed issue.
sentences.zh: 平心而论，问题的关键不在于高速公路的建筑设计。

sentences.en: I'm just trying to think creatively.
sentences.zh: 我只是试着发挥创意想一想。

sentences.en: I'm just trying to think of ways that the Second World War could have been stopped.
sentences.zh: 我只是在想有没有什么办法能阻止第二次世界大战。

sentences.en: Of course you are.
sentences.zh: 你当然会这么想。

sentences.en: Neville Chamberlain joins us now on the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 内维尔·张伯伦现在加入了我们的播客。

sentences.en: Just trying to think creatively.
sentences.zh: 只是试着发挥创意想一想。

sentences.en: We're going to hear him from Lord Halifax now.
sentences.zh: 我们现在要听听哈利法克斯勋爵怎么说。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Well, because, I mean, let's face it, the consequences of the Poles deciding that they're going to resist German aggression for Poland.
sentences.zh: 因为，咱们面对现实吧，波兰人决定反抗德国对波兰的侵略，其后果……

sentences.en: It's disastrous.
sentences.zh: 是灾难性的。

sentences.en: And for millions and millions of Poles, and especially Jewish Poles, I mean, is literally genocidal.
sentences.zh: 对于数以百万计的波兰人，尤其是波兰犹太人来说，这简直是种族灭绝。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They are.
sentences.zh: 他们确实是。

sentences.en: But I'm just wondering whether there was any possibility of a kind of modus operandi that could have been struck.
sentences.zh: 但我只是在想，是否有可能达成某种折衷方案。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: And the reason is because if they do this, they turn themselves completely into a satellite of Germany, which they are never, ever, ever going to do.
sentences.zh: 原因在于，如果他们这么做了，他们就完全变成了德国的附庸，而这是他们永远、永远、永远都不会做的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: They think if we give them Danzig, we totally lose control of our trade.
sentences.zh: 他们认为，如果我们把但泽给他们，我们就彻底失去了对贸易的控制权。

sentences.en: Germany will now control everything we export and everything we import because it has to go through this port, pretty much.
sentences.zh: 德国现在将控制我们所有的出口和进口，因为货物基本上都得经过这个港口。

sentences.en: Or if it's going to go by land, it's got to go through Germany.
sentences.zh: 或者如果走陆路，也必须经过德国。

sentences.en: So we just turn ourselves completely into a puppet.
sentences.zh: 所以我们只是把自己彻底变成了傀儡。

sentences.en: If we join the anti-comintern pact, you know, we are on Germany's side against Russia.
sentences.zh: 如果我们加入《反共产国际协定》，你知道，我们就站在德国一边反对俄国了。

sentences.en: Again, we lose control of our foreign policy.
sentences.zh: 同样，我们失去了外交政策的控制权。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And they're bordering Russia.
sentences.zh: 而且他们与俄国接壤。

sentences.en: We're not going to do that.
sentences.zh: 我们不会那么做的。

sentences.en: The point is Polish independence, which they fought for, which their forefathers have fought for for more than a century.
sentences.zh: 重点是波兰的独立，这是他们为之奋斗的目标，也是他们的先辈一个多世纪以来为之奋斗的目标。

sentences.en: They're not going to give that away, you know, like that.
sentences.zh: 他们不会就这样轻易放弃的。

sentences.en: Now, Hitler at first thinks, oh, the Poles, they're being very difficult.
sentences.zh: 希特勒起初认为，哦，波兰人，他们真是太难缠了。

sentences.en: But he doesn't immediately think I'm going to attack them.
sentences.zh: 但他并没有立刻想到要攻击他们。

sentences.en: He thinks they will see sense eventually.
sentences.zh: 他认为他们最终会认清现实。

sentences.en: He invites Beck to the Eagle's NeSt.
sentences.zh: 他邀请贝克去鹰巢。

sentences.en: Beck goes along to the Eagle's Nest where Chamberlain went.
sentences.zh: 贝克去了张伯伦也去过的鹰巢。

sentences.en: And Beck says, look, you know, I can't help you.
sentences.zh: 贝克说，听着，你知道，我帮不了你。

sentences.en: Polish public opinion will not allow us to give you these concessions.
sentences.zh: 波兰的公众舆论不会允许我们做出这些让步。

sentences.en: At this point, Hitler hasn't yet entered Prague.
sentences.zh: 此时，希特勒还没有进入布拉格。

sentences.en: So he says to his aides, well, when I crush Czechoslovakia and I enter Prague, that will frighten the Poles and they will be more cooperative.
sentences.zh: 所以他告诉他的助手，好吧，等我摧毁捷克斯洛伐克并进入布拉格，那会吓坏波兰人，他们就会更配合了。

sentences.en: So let's see if it does.
sentences.zh: 让我们看看是不是这样。

sentences.en: Let's go forward in time to March.
sentences.zh: 让我们把时间推到三月。

sentences.en: Six days after Hitler has entered Prague as a conqueror, Ribbentrop again meets the
sentences.zh: 在希特勒以征服者身份进入布拉格六天后，里宾特洛甫再次会见了

sentences.en: Polish ambassador and he says, right, I need Beck to come to Berlin.
sentences.zh: 波兰大使，他说，好了，我需要贝克来柏林。

sentences.en: We're running out of patience.
sentences.zh: 我们的耐心快耗尽了。

sentences.en: Our newspapers have had enough.
sentences.zh: 我们的报纸已经受够了。

sentences.en: They're really putting pressure on us.
sentences.zh: 他们真的在给我们施压。

sentences.en: If you give us Danzig, maybe we'll give you a little bit of Slovakia.
sentences.zh: 如果你把但泽给我们，也许我们会给你一点斯洛伐克领土。

sentences.en: We'll get a bit of Ukraine for you or something.
sentences.zh: 我们会为你弄点乌克兰领土之类的。

sentences.en: Tell Beck to come anyway.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，告诉贝克来一趟。

sentences.en: We'll talk to him about it.
sentences.zh: 我们会和他谈谈这件事。

sentences.en: And the ambassador five days later says, you know, Beck's not going to come.
sentences.zh: 五天后，大使说，你知道，贝克不会来的。

sentences.en: He doesn't want to come.
sentences.zh: 他不想来。

sentences.en: You're not interested.
sentences.zh: 你根本不感兴趣。

sentences.en: He says he's not interested in anything that you could possibly offer him.
sentences.zh: 他说他对你可能提供的任何东西都不感兴趣。

sentences.en: And if you attack us, we'll fight you.
sentences.zh: 如果你攻击我们，我们就会反击。

sentences.en: Now, you may say, this is your point here, Tom.
sentences.zh: 现在，你可能会说，这就是你的观点，汤姆。

sentences.en: This is reckless.
sentences.zh: 这太鲁莽了。

sentences.en: This is incredibly bold.
sentences.zh: 这极其大胆。

sentences.en: Beck's argument and the Poles' argument is, we saw what happened to Czechoslovakia.
sentences.zh: 贝克的论点和波兰人的论点是，我们看到了捷克斯洛伐克发生了什么。

sentences.en: I'm aware that I am being inconsistent here because I've been encouraging the Czechs to resiSt.
sentences.zh: 我知道我在这里前后矛盾，因为我一直在鼓励捷克人反抗。

sentences.en: But I suppose also at this point, the Poles think that they're only facing a conflict on one of their borders.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，此时波兰人也认为他们只需要面对其中一个边境的冲突。

sentences.en: They are indeed.
sentences.zh: 他们确实是这么想的。

sentences.en: They don't think there's any possibility of, say, an alliance between the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 他们认为苏联之间根本不可能结盟。

sentences.en: They absolutely don't.
sentences.zh: 他们绝对不这么认为。

sentences.en: The Poles think, look, we saw with the Czechs what happened when you appease Hitler.
sentences.zh: 波兰人想，看，我们从捷克人身上看到了绥靖希特勒的后果。

sentences.en: When you give in to him, he just nibbles more and more and more and eventually he comes back for the lot.
sentences.zh: 当你向他屈服时，他只会一点一点地蚕食，最终他会把一切都夺走。

sentences.en: But the only way to stand up to him is just to draw a red line and to say no, and then maybe he'll back off.
sentences.zh: 但对抗他的唯一方法就是划定红线并说不，也许他就会退缩。

sentences.en: And Beck gives this amazing speech, actually, to the same, which is the Polish parliament.
sentences.zh: 贝克在波兰议会发表了那场精彩的演讲。

sentences.en: He says, peace is a precious and desirable thing.
sentences.zh: 他说，和平是一件珍贵且令人向往的事物。

sentences.en: And that's the attitude that a Prussian nobleman should respect.
sentences.zh: 而这正是普鲁士贵族应该尊重的态度。

sentences.en: And it reflects poorly on Prussian noblemen.
sentences.zh: 但这在普鲁士贵族身上体现得很差劲。

sentences.en: They don't respect it in this case.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，他们并不尊重这一点。

sentences.en: Now, Beck is confident that he can back this up because he has sent feelers out to London saying, will you back me up here?
sentences.zh: 现在，贝克很有信心他能支撑住，因为他已经向伦敦试探过了，问他们是否会支持他。

sentences.en: Please, will you support me?
sentences.zh: 请问，你们会支持我吗？

sentences.en: Now, we heard before the break, Chamberlain has already changed his policy and he thinks we need to deter Hitler.
sentences.zh: 我们之前在休息前听到了，张伯伦已经改变了他的政策，他认为我们需要威慑希特勒。

sentences.en: And his military chiefs are quite keen on an alliance with Poland because, of course, what they want is if there's a war with Hitler,
sentences.zh: 他的军事首长们非常热衷于与波兰结盟，因为当然，他们想要的是如果与希特勒开战，

sentences.en: they want Hitler to be fighting on two fronts, west and eaSt.
sentences.zh: 他们希望希特勒在东西两线作战。

sentences.en: But, of course, there's no, I mean, real practical possibility of British armed aid reaching Poland.
sentences.zh: 但当然，英国的武装援助实际上不可能到达波兰。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不可能。

sentences.en: And we will come to this in the next couple of episodes that, unfortunately,
sentences.zh: 我们会在接下来的几集里谈到这一点，不幸的是，

sentences.en: there is a difference of opinion between London and Warsaw about whether or not Britain can actually help Poland.
sentences.zh: 伦敦和华沙对于英国是否真的能帮助波兰存在分歧。

sentences.en: As we shall see, Britain doesn't.
sentences.zh: 正如我们将看到的，英国并没有做到。

sentences.en: Now, the French are also keen on an alliance with Poland.
sentences.zh: 现在，法国人也热衷于与波兰结盟。

sentences.en: They've got a long history of friendship and Deladier says to London, yeah, we'll fight for Danzig.
sentences.zh: 他们有着悠久的友谊历史，达拉第对伦敦说，是的，我们会为但泽而战。

sentences.en: You know, that's our red line.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那是我们的红线。

sentences.en: That's fine.
sentences.zh: 没问题。

sentences.en: That's the context for Chamberlain going to the House of Commons on the 31st of March 1939 and delivering his famous guarantee that if Polish independence is threatened and if Poland resists,
sentences.zh: 这就是张伯伦在1939年3月31日前往下议院发表他那著名保证的背景，即如果波兰的独立受到威胁且波兰进行抵抗，

sentences.en: his majesty's government would feel themselves bound at once to lend the Polish government all support in their power.
sentences.zh: 国王陛下政府将感到有义务立即向波兰政府提供他们能力范围内的所有支持。

sentences.en: Now, you made this point just a second ago.
sentences.zh: 你刚才提到了这一点。

sentences.en: What does that actually mean?
sentences.zh: 那到底意味着什么？

sentences.en: Like, what could the British actually do?
sentences.zh: 比如，英国人实际上能做什么？

sentences.en: Britain is a long way from Poland and Germany is in the way.
sentences.zh: 英国离波兰很远，中间还隔着德国。

sentences.en: So, realistically, what can we do?
sentences.zh: 所以，现实地讲，我们能做什么？

sentences.en: And actually, even at this point, Chamberlain's military chief say to him, if Hitler does attack Poland, we're probably not going to do anything.
sentences.zh: 事实上，即使在这一点上，张伯伦的军事首长也告诉他，如果希特勒真的攻击波兰，我们可能什么也做不了。

sentences.en: There's nothing much we can practically do to help the Poles.
sentences.zh: 我们在实际行动上帮不了波兰什么忙。

sentences.en: But I suppose what Chamberlain would say in his defense is he doesn't see this as a last step, but as a first step.
sentences.zh: 但我猜张伯伦会为自己辩解说，他并不认为这是最后一步，而是第一步。

sentences.en: So, he is thinking we'll get Poland, then we'll maybe get Romania in an alliance and ideally maybe the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 所以，他在想我们会争取到波兰，然后也许会争取到罗马尼亚结盟，理想情况下也许还有苏联。

sentences.en: Well, because that was the card that he could potentially have played over the Czech crisis, but doesn't.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为那是他在捷克危机中本可以打出的一张牌，但他没有。

sentences.en: I mean, that's the one card, I'm guessing, that Hitler would have...
sentences.zh: 我是说，我猜那是希特勒会……的一张牌。

sentences.en: Yes, agreed.
sentences.zh: 是的，同意。

sentences.en: Of course, that's a very difficult card for any British government, especially a conservative government, to play.
sentences.zh: 当然，这对任何英国政府，尤其是保守党政府来说，都是一张非常难打的牌。

sentences.en: They regard the Soviet Union really as the ideological arch enemy and have done for 20 years.
sentences.zh: 他们一直把苏联视为意识形态上的死敌，已经20年了。

sentences.en: You know, the Bolshevik, Stalin's regime, a blood-soaked regime, rumours, reports of the Great Terror coming out.
sentences.zh: 你知道，布尔什维克，斯大林的政权，一个血腥的政权，传言，关于大清洗的报道传了出来。

sentences.en: There's been rumours of the famine in Ukraine and the Holodmoor.
sentences.zh: 有关于乌克兰大饥荒和乌克兰大饥荒的传言。

sentences.en: You know, there are big obstacles to a deal with the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 你知道，与苏联达成协议存在巨大的障碍。

sentences.en: And one of the biggest, by the way, is the Poles.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，其中最大的障碍之一就是波兰人。

sentences.en: The Poles, when they hear talk of this, they're like, what?
sentences.zh: 波兰人听到这种说法时，他们会说，什么？

sentences.en: The Russians?
sentences.zh: 俄国人？

sentences.en: We hate the Russians.
sentences.zh: 我们讨厌俄国人。

sentences.en: No way are we doing an alliance with the Russians.
sentences.zh: 我们绝不可能与俄国人结盟。

sentences.en: Are the British and the French, they're sufficiently alert to the fact that the Soviet Union is the great object of Nazi hatred?
sentences.zh: 英国人和法国人是否充分意识到苏联是纳粹仇恨的主要目标？

sentences.en: Yeah, they know that.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们知道。

sentences.en: They know that Hitler has rancid and raved about the Soviet Union for, you know, more than a decade.
sentences.zh: 他们知道希特勒十多年来一直对苏联咆哮和谩骂。

sentences.en: So the Soviet Union is quite keen on the idea of the capitalist powers fighting themselves.
sentences.zh: 所以苏联对资本主义大国自相残杀的想法很感兴趣。

sentences.en: So Britain, France and Germany.
sentences.zh: 也就是英国、法国和德国。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, is there any enthusiasm in Paris and London for the notion that the Nazis and the Soviets fight each other and we just sit back and watch them?
sentences.zh: 我是说，巴黎和伦敦对于纳粹和苏联互相残杀，而我们只是坐在一旁观看的想法有什么热情吗？

sentences.en: Somebody at Neville Chamberlain would have said to you, that's the dream.
sentences.zh: 内维尔·张伯伦手下的某个人会对你说，那简直是梦想。

sentences.en: That basically they'll destroy each other.
sentences.zh: 基本上他们会互相摧毁。

sentences.en: They're both terrible regimes and I hope they fight and I hope they both lose.
sentences.zh: 这两个政权都很糟糕，我希望他们打起来，也希望他们两败俱伤。

sentences.en: That's exactly what a lot of people in Britain and indeed in France would have said, I should say.
sentences.zh: 我得说，这正是当时英国乃至法国许多人会说的话。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Does the Polish alliance complicate that?
sentences.zh: 波兰的结盟会使情况复杂化吗？

sentences.en: Because obviously Poland lies between Germany and the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 因为很显然，波兰位于德国和苏联之间。

sentences.en: So if they're allying with Poland, that complicates that strategy.
sentences.zh: 所以如果他们与波兰结盟，那就会使这一战略复杂化。

sentences.en: So I think at this point, in March 1939, when they give the guarantee, they realise, of course, the next war is not going to be Hitler versus Stalin.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为在1939年3月这个时间点，当他们提供保证时，他们当然意识到下一场战争不会是希特勒对阵斯大林。

sentences.en: The war that they're trying to avert is Hitler versus Poland.
sentences.zh: 他们试图避免的战争是希特勒对阵波兰。

sentences.en: So Hitler versus Stalin is off the table as a war, realistically, at that point.
